union.statement: Internal cross-reference '§2.6' (cited 3x: REC-GOAL-4 line 72, REC-LIFE-2 line 94, REC-LIFE-6 line 122) does not exist; §2 ends at §2.4, which is the data-tables section actually meant.
Internal cross-reference '§6.1' (cited 3x: lines 89, 98, 359) does not exist; §6 has no subsections and the attrition metric is REC-GATE-1.
Ruling §7c.16 (per-model spacing deleted; global 10s dispatch gap) appears nowhere in the spec body or the §8 traceability table, despite §8's header claiming no ruling is silently dropped.
Ruling §7c.17 (dispatcher predicate) is honored in the spec body (REC-LIFE-6) but is absent from the §8 traceability table.

Ruling §7c.15's condition (b) -- a dedicated security analysis of the runaway surface before build -- is unaddressed anywhere in S04, S01/pass2, or S03; condition (a) (descriptive constant renames) was separately discharged by ruling §7c.18.
Rulings §7c.27-30 postdate the spec's stated input window ('rulings 11-26') and are not folded into §8 or the body; the spec's Inputs line only ever claimed 11-26.

§8 maps §7c.13 (short-name resolution/retirement re-pointing semantics) to 'REC-LIFE-9 (table note)', but that table note only restates ruling 11's per-model-not-per-family point -- ruling 13's actual content (always resolves to latest active version; retirement re-points, never rewrites) is absent from the spec text entirely.

Three §-ref pointers resolve to the wrong section though the content exists elsewhere: decision-log.md §2 cited for T568-4/T557-1 (actually §5, 'Full row table'); S03-queue-layer/spec.md §3 cited for the queue-cycle 'tail step' (the iteration order is actually §8); S03 §3 cited (bundled) for FLEET_MODEL_DENY/ALLOW (actually §1's R9 row, line 128).

REC-ESC-7 cites 'sprint.md audit loop' as authority for a third-audit cap, but sprint.md's audit-loop section still states a two-round cap; the cap-3 rule actually comes from ruling §7c.21, which supersedes sprint.md but is not named as the citation.

REC-CTRL-1 claims 'every id in §1-§4 has at least one arm here [in the C1-C10 table]', but the table's flip column names only 10 distinct ids of the 28 normative ids in §1-§4 (18 uncovered, 14 of 24 excluding the four definitional REC-GOAL statements).

§6 (REC-GATE-1..4 -- the attrition metric and the retirement gate, this sprint's stated 'verification centerpiece') sits entirely outside REC-CTRL-1's stated '§1-§4' scope and has no arm in C1-C10 or any other stated verification regime; by §0's own rule ('an id with no control is not a requirement, it is a wish') the retirement gate is currently a wish.

The deferred-to-design run-record schema (§7) lists only generic fields (wake id, residue, verdict, probe flag, token count, wall, '§6.1 metric fields') and omits the specific evidence AUTOPILOT-5H's own gate needs to compute (orphans, runaways, breaker-trips, panics, per-run delegation/resolution/close counts).
'Unattended' (REC-GATE-2) and 'thrash' (REC-GATE-2's zero-list and REC-ESC-3's panic-halt trigger) are used as pass/fail gate criteria but are nowhere defined in the spec.

REC-GATE-2 states the ACTIVE-autopilot bar per-hour ('each of the five hours must contain real delegation, issue resolution, and closes') while REC-GATE-4 operationalizes it per-run ('each run must show at least one delegation, one issue resolution, and one close') -- a run with all activity in hour one satisfies REC-GATE-4 and fails REC-GATE-2's literal reading.

REC-GOAL-4 claims the 12 (b) decisions are 'discharged by data tables that already exist', but REC-LIFE-9 rows only 9 of 12 (provider-quota 7 + ordering 2); decision-log's other two (b) sub-categories -- model-fit (2) and measurement-validity (1) -- have no table row anywhere in the spec.

REC-VERB-4 states caller identity must be kernel-attested 'never from an env-var self-declaration', naming MANAGENT_TASK_ID as spoofable -- but the prerequisite pass-2 spec S04 gates its build on still resolves worker-vs-operator identity via a disjunction (MANAGENT_TASK_ID set OR the held-child marker) whose negation reads the caller as the OPERATOR, a privilege-granting fallback with no registered fold closing the gap ruling §7c.18(a) names.

REC-VERB-2's never-list forbids the reconciler from 'editing a spec/plan', but REC-VERB-4 locates all enforcement in managent's mutating-verb refusal -- a spec/plan file edit is a raw filesystem write via Edit/Write, not a managent verb, so managent cannot mechanically refuse it, and no other mechanism (holds=, pre-commit hook) is named for this specific case.

REC-LIFE-8 makes --holds mandatory at every mint with no stated exception, while REC-VERB-3 (the reconciler's one permitted mint, a read-only investigation lane) by construction holds no file -- the reconciler's only legal mint is refused by its own stated prerequisite, with no explicit 'no holds' sentinel defined.

REC-GATE-3 asserts 'L1 and this gate are one bar, not two' while enumerating a conjunction that differs from the ratified §7b.9 L1 bar in three terms: it drops 'acceptance-suite PASS', drops 'fleet display accurate against ps', and drops the 'managent landmark L1 --declare' action, while adding a new term ('every escalation in-contract') absent from §7b.9.

The attrition metric is stated once as a general efficiency ratio (REC-GATE-1: fraction of wakes needing zero tokens) and again in language that reads as measuring a specific failure (REC-LIFE-1: 'spawning a model for [an empty-residue wake] is the failure this spec's attrition metric measures') -- a failure REC-LIFE-2's own pre-pass design makes structurally impossible, so the two statements should be reconciled to one definition in one place.

Ruling §7c.23's second clause ('an agent that challenges epistemology MUST propose testable hypotheses and actually test them') is not absorbed anywhere in S04; REC-VERB-6 covers only the first clause (no gate/brief/acceptance edits).

REC-ESC-5's routing rule ('route the blocking file to its owning row, derived from holds=/the store, never the reconciler's guess') has no seeded control arm -- C10 tests only the 'report is forbidden as a category' half, not the actual file-to-owner routing mechanism, which decision-log F7 records as the harder of the two historical blocker shapes.

REC-CTRL-3 names T572 as the store-write prerequisite gating the reconciler's first live wake, but ruling §7c.30 names a different task, T587, for the same gate; T572 and T587 are different defect classes (load-test store-pollution vs. store-write UTF-8 byte-correctness). Both are now closed, so no live build risk remains, but the citation is still the wrong task.

adjudication.citation: docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:72,94,122 cite '§2.6'; the document's §2 subsections run 2.1-2.4 only (spec.md:144 '## 2.4 The data tables'), and no §2.5/§2.6 exists anywhere in the file.
adjudication.why: Verified by direct read: no §2.5 or §2.6 heading exists; §2.4 is unambiguously the intended target (its own title matches 'the data tables'). Cheap, unambiguous fix, but a real defect under the spec's own citation-pin rule.

adjudication.citation: docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:89,98,359 cite '§6.1'; §6 (line 306) has no subsections -- the attrition metric is REC-GATE-1 (line 308).
adjudication.why: Verified by direct read of §6: it runs REC-GATE-1..4 with no numbered subsections. Same class of defect as U1, different target.

adjudication.citation: grep for 'spacing|dispatch gap' over spec.md returns zero hits; §8's table (spec.md:379-398) has no row for §7c.16; ruling 16 itself is at docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:149-156.
adjudication.why: The content is defensibly delegated -- REC-VERB-1 dispatches only via the supervisor (managent supervise), so the 10s stampede guard is enforced upstream in S03/pass-2 -- but the delegation is never stated, which breaks §8's own 'no ruling silently dropped' contract. Mechanical, one-line fix.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:119 'must pass the dispatcher predicate' (REC-LIFE-6); §8's table (spec.md:379-398) has no §7c.17 row.
adjudication.why: Substance is correctly present in the body; this is purely an index-completeness gap in §8, not a missing requirement.

adjudication.citation: docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:141-144 (ruling 15, condition (b): 'a dedicated security analysis of the runaway surface before build'); grep for 'security analysis|threat model' across spec.md, seed.md, decision-log.md, S01 pass2 spec, and S03 spec returns no matching hit tied to this condition.
adjudication.why: This is a ratified, explicit pre-build condition on the exact runaway/mint-safety surface the reconciler's verb boundary rests on (REC-VERB-3, REC-VERB-4), and it is owned by nobody in any of the three specs S04's build gating (§7) names. Condition (a) of the same ruling (descriptive names) was separately and correctly discharged by ruling §7c.18's renames, so only (b) is the live gap.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:14 ('orchestration-layer-spec.md §7c rulings 11-26'); rulings 27-28 committed at 9efa218 and 29-30 at f79f53d ('commit operator rulings §7c 29-30', per git log), both after the spec's own citation pin 14d8d6b.
adjudication.why: The spec explicitly scopes its own inputs to rulings 11-26 and the later rulings postdate that pin by minutes to hours on the same day -- this is disclosed, expected staleness with a fold owed at the next rev, not a silent-drop defect at the pin itself.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:151 (REC-LIFE-9 appetite row) states only '0-9 per model short name, not per family' -- ruling 11's content; ruling 13's actual text is at docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:131-134 ('short names ALWAYS resolve to the latest actively used version...retiring a model re-points the short name; it never rewrites history') and does not appear anywhere in spec.md.
adjudication.why: §8 asserts coverage ('REC-LIFE-9 (table note)') that the cited text does not contain. A false 'covered' entry is worse than an honest gap because it stops the next auditor from looking -- correctly flagged as a should-fix, not blocking, since nothing in S04's own verb set currently depends on short-name retirement semantics.

adjudication.citation: decision-log.md §2 ('The counted table', line 50) vs §5 ('Full row table', line 184) -- T568-4/T557-1 rows are at lines 337/326, under §5; S03-queue-layer/spec.md §3 ('Conditions', line 320) vs §8 ('The iteration, in order', line 1191); FLEET_MODEL_DENY/ALLOW is documented at S03 spec.md:128, under §1 ('Recovery'), not §3.
adjudication.why: Content exists and is substantively correct at every target; only the section pointer is imprecise in three places. Low-impact, mechanical fix.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:264 cites 'sprint.md audit loop' for the third-audit cap; docs/infra/sprint.md:105 states 'Two-round cap for document review.' The cap-3 rule is at docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:183-192 (ruling §7c.21).
adjudication.why: A reader who checks the named source (sprint.md) finds a number that contradicts the spec's own stated cap, with no note that ruling §7c.21 supersedes it. The ruling itself is correctly followed; only the citation is wrong.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:271-286: counting the 'flips' column of C1-C10 yields exactly 10 distinct ids (REC-LIFE-1, REC-LIFE-2, REC-VERB-1, REC-VERB-4, REC-VERB-5, REC-VERB-6, REC-VERB-7, REC-ESC-1, REC-ESC-2, REC-ESC-5); §1-§4 declare 28 normative ids (REC-GOAL-1..4, REC-LIFE-1..9, REC-VERB-1..8, REC-ESC-1..7).
adjudication.why: Directly countable and confirmed: 18 of 28 ids have no arm in the printed table, including REC-VERB-2 (the never-list), REC-VERB-3 (the one permitted mint), REC-VERB-8 (templated directives), and REC-LIFE-8 (the mint refusal the sprint calls its highest-yield fix). The sentence 'every id in §1-§4 has at least one arm here' is a direct overclaim about control coverage, which this project's own standing doctrine treats as the failure mode to guard against hardest.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:33-36 (§0's blanket rule, scoped by REC-CTRL-1 to '§1-§4', spec.md:271); §6 (REC-GATE-1..4, lines 306-337) sits outside that window with no arm in C1-C10 and no other stated verification regime.
adjudication.why: By the document's own literal wording the retirement gate is currently 'a wish, not a requirement'. Mitigating factor (noted by two lanes independently): AUTOPILOT-5H is inherently a live multi-run measurement, not a scratch-store unit test, so the C1-C10 shape genuinely does not fit it -- but the spec never says so, which is the actual defect: either restate §0's scope explicitly or give §6 its own named verification regime.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:356-359 lists the run-record schema's required fields: 'wake id, residue, verdict per action, probe flag, token count, wall, and the §6.1 metric fields' -- no field named for orphans, runaways, breaker-trips, panics, or REC-GATE-4's per-run delegation/resolution/close counts.
adjudication.why: The schema is explicitly deferred to design, so this is not yet a build-blocking gap, but a gate whose own evidence fields are absent from the schema it mandates cannot be computed once built -- should be added to the deferred-field list now while it is cheap.

adjudication.citation: 'unattended' appears only at spec.md:315 (REC-GATE-2) and 'thrash' at spec.md:242-244 (REC-ESC-3) and spec.md:332-337 (REC-GATE-4's zero-list) -- neither term has a definition anywhere in the document (grep-verified).
adjudication.why: Both are load-bearing in pass/fail gates ('thrash' doubles as the panic-halt trigger), so an undefined term here is a real gate-scriptability gap. Should be fixed before the AUTOPILOT-5H control arm (U11) is written, since the arm cannot be scripted against an undefined term.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:318 (REC-GATE-2: 'each of the five hours must contain real delegation, issue resolution, and closes') vs spec.md:333-334 (REC-GATE-4: 'each AUTOPILOT-5H run must show at least one delegation, one issue resolution, and one close').
adjudication.why: Verified by direct comparison of the two clauses -- one is a per-hour requirement (5 required occurrences per run), the other is a per-run requirement (1 required occurrence per run). These are materially different bars for the sprint's own stated 'verification centerpiece', and as written the gate cannot be scripted until one wins.

adjudication.citation: docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/decision-log.md:86-89 breaks (b) into provider-quota/appetite (7), model-fit (2), ordering (2), measurement-validity (1) = 12; spec.md:146-153 (REC-LIFE-9) rows only appetite, provider-quota/cooldown, and ordering.
adjudication.why: 9 of 12 (b) rows are demonstrably tabled (provider-quota 7 + ordering 2); model-fit (2) is only loosely gestured at via REC-LIFE-6's 'should use' language and measurement-validity (1) has no home anywhere in the spec. REC-GOAL-4's blanket claim ('discharged by data tables that already exist') overstates this by 3 of 12 rows -- the 19.4% scope number itself is unaffected.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:184-191 (REC-VERB-4, citing MANAGENT_TASK_ID as spoofable-by-unsetting); docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S01-process-ownership/pass2/spec.md:762-766 ('A caller with MANAGENT_TASK_ID set (or the supervisor's held-child marker) is a worker...A caller without it is the operator...minted_by = operator').
adjudication.why: Verified directly: pass-2 §5's N5 rule treats absence of BOTH signals as the operator, a privilege-granting fallback, not an unidentified-caller refusal. For a legitimately supervisor-spawned reconciler the held-child marker persists independent of the env var, so this is not demonstrated as a live exploit against REC-VERB-4's own design -- but it is a real, unregistered fold gap between a ratified security Must (§7c.18(a)) and the prerequisite spec S04's build gate (§7) depends on.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:169-172 (REC-VERB-2's never-list includes 'edit a spec/plan'); spec.md:184-191 (REC-VERB-4: 'the verb boundary lives in managent itself, exactly as MANAGENT_TEST=1 refuses mutating verbs today').
adjudication.why: Editing a document is a filesystem write via Edit/Write, not a managent verb call -- managent has no mechanism to intercept it. The spec names holds=/one-writer and the pre-commit hook nowhere as the actual enforcement for this specific never-list item, and C6 (spec.md:282) only probes a brief instructing amend/retire, not a file edit.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:136-138 (REC-LIFE-8: '...a row minted without a holds declaration is refused at write time'); spec.md:178-180 (REC-VERB-3: 'read-only -- it may not mutate the store beyond its own close').
adjudication.why: This is a self-contained logical contradiction within the document itself, independent of any external source: a mint that holds no file (REC-VERB-3, by construction) cannot satisfy a mandatory-holds-at-mint rule (REC-LIFE-8) unless an explicit sentinel (e.g. '--holds none') is defined, and none is. As spec'd, the reconciler's one legal mint is refused by its own stated prerequisite.

adjudication.citation: docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:99-103 (ruling §7b.9: acceptance PASS 3 days, zero relays, duties current, fleet display accurate against ps, every gauge reproducible, then landmark L1 --declare, independently audited) vs spec.md:325-330 (REC-GATE-3: 3 clean days, zero relays, duties current, every escalation in-contract, every gauge reproducible, independently audited).
adjudication.why: Verified term-by-term: REC-GATE-3 drops 'acceptance-suite PASS', drops 'fleet display accurate against ps', and drops the 'landmark L1 --declare' action step, while adding a new term ('every escalation in-contract') not in §7b.9. This is the literal, irreversible seat-retirement criterion (REC-GATE-3: 'the seat ends...no successor minted'); a differing conjunction that omits two ratified terms means the new gate could be satisfied while the ratified L1 bar is not, contradicting the spec's own 'one bar, not two' claim.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:308-313 (REC-GATE-1: fraction of wakes needing zero tokens, framed as a general efficiency ratio) vs spec.md:88-89 (REC-LIFE-1: 'spawning a model for [an empty-residue wake] is the failure this spec's attrition metric...measures') and spec.md:91-99 (REC-LIFE-2: on empty residue 'no model is spawned', making the named failure structurally impossible by the very mechanism that measures it).
adjudication.why: A real definitional muddle between the two passages, but low practical stakes -- REC-GATE-1 is the operative definition and is internally coherent on its own; REC-LIFE-1's phrasing should be tightened to cross-reference rather than restate.

adjudication.citation: docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:206-207 (ruling §7c.23's second clause) vs spec.md:202-206 (REC-VERB-6, covering only the gate/brief/acceptance-edit clause) and spec.md:196-200 (REC-VERB-5: 'the reconciler never invents a verdict -- it runs the declared gate or routes the audit and records the verdict').
adjudication.why: The spec does not settle whether the second clause needed separate treatment: REC-VERB-5's existing constraint (no invented verdicts) plausibly already forecloses accepting an untested epistemology challenge as satisfying a gate, but the spec never states this connection explicitly, so it is genuinely ambiguous rather than a clear miss.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:246-251 (REC-ESC-5's routing rule) vs spec.md:283 (control C10: 'a "report" escalation | refused as a category; managent done is the record | REC-ESC-5').
adjudication.why: C10's expected behavior column tests only the 'report forbidden' half of REC-ESC-5; there is no seeded arm exercising the actual routing decision (deriving the owning row from holds=/the store for a real cross-lane blocker), which decision-log.md's F7 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/decision-log.md, F7 entry) records as the harder of the two historically-observed blocker shapes.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:293-295 (REC-CTRL-3 names T572); docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:249-250 (ruling §7c.30 names T587); docs/infra/managent/tasks.json entries for T572 ('untracked/T572-load-test-store-pollution.md') and T587 ('untracked/T587-store-write-utf8.md') confirm these are distinct tasks/defect classes, both status=done, verdict=pass-with-findings.
adjudication.why: The citation names the wrong task relative to what the ruling specifies, but since both T572 and T587 are independently verified closed (pass-with-findings), there is no live build risk today -- purely a stale/wrong citation to fix at the next rev.

notes: Adjudication of five anonymized, shuffled lane audits (untracked/race-f/lanes/lane-1..5.json) of docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md (author DSPro/T582). Lane-2 was independently confirmed to be my own prior audit (findings/T588-race-a-sonnet.json, byte-identical notes text) -- expected per the brief, and treated as one lane's vote like any other, not given extra weight. 23 union items were identified across the five lanes' findings/notes text. Every 'real' or 'false' verdict below was checked directly against the cited primary source (spec.md, docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md §7c rulings 11-30, decision-log.md §2/§5, sprint.md, S01-process-ownership/pass2/spec.md §4.4/§5, S03-queue-layer/spec.md §1/§3/§8, and docs/infra/managent/tasks.json for T572/T587 status) -- not from lane agreement or vote count, per the brief's bar. One item (U21) is adjudicated uncertain because the spec's text does not settle it either way. No item was found to be outright false as raised, though one adjacent claim not promoted to a union item (a lane's assertion that 'runaway_streak mechanism is never mentioned in spec') is contradicted by spec.md:364, which does name and cite the ratified value (the fuller *mechanism* definition is correctly left unrestated, consistent with REC-LIFE-9's 'consumed, not re-derived' design) -- omitted from the union as not a distinct defect once checked. Five items (U5, U10, U14, U18, U19) are adjudicated 'must': an unaddressed ratified pre-build security condition (U5), a direct overclaim about control-battery coverage against the project's own anti-green-test doctrine (U10), a literal per-hour-vs-per-run contradiction in the sprint's stated verification centerpiece (U14), a self-contained logical contradiction between two Musts in the same document (U18), and a seat-retirement gate whose stated 'one bar, not two' claim demonstrably differs from the ratified bar it claims to equal (U19). No findings file writes were made outside this deliverable; the spec, the lane files, and race-grading/ were not touched. Inbox polled at claim and before done: empty both times, no directive IDs to record.
